title: What a model may read: business examples v2, with a visibility and the owner's pattern fields
request: Phase 8, Part C (the owner, after the design session on their retail interview): build the knowledge, cards and recipes plan non-stop; the repository is private now, but no model ever sees the owner's fraud data, and a model reads patterns, not people's names.
plan: Move the business-example contract to v2 with a visibility (model or rules_only) and read every stored v1 example.
Add the owner's pattern card fields in the same version (one contract bump for 30.7 and 30.8): the pattern, practice questions, the recipe link, the replicas.
Make the owner's fraud solution rules_only and give every model reader one filter (for_model) and one context builder (context_for_model).
Keep where an example is stored and the raw conversation out of what a role reads.

decisions.decision: One contract version carries both the visibility and the pattern fields.
decisions.why: The rule is one contract bump per commit; 30.8 fills the fields 30.7 defines, so splitting them would bump the version twice for one shape.

decisions.decision: An owner's solution can never be visible to a model, and a stored v1 one reads as rules_only.
decisions.why: The default visibility is model; a forgotten flag on a second owner solution, or an older export read by a newer library, would put private findings in a model's context.

decisions.decision: The practice questions are kept out of the search index.
decisions.why: They are the evaluation set of the search: a question indexed into its own example finds that example by construction.

decisions.decision: Without the owner's folder beside the repository, a rebuild keeps the committed owner example.
decisions.why: A worktree or another machine has no copy of the owner's folder; dropping the example there would silently remove what the rules read.

change: dclab_core.business_examples v2 (dclab-core 0.75.0: visibility, owner_document, Pattern, Practice, RecipeLink, replicas, for_model); dclab_rnd/business_examples.py (rules_only owner example, context_for_model, the template track skipped, the committed owner example kept); tests/test_business_examples.py; the schema baseline v2; evidence/business_examples rebuilt.

findings.defect: The knowledge base read the new-track template as a research track.
findings.scenario: The freshness test, written first, showed an example titled with the template's placeholder among the tracks.
findings.cause: The builder globbed every research folder, the template included, where the research map skips names starting with an underscore.
findings.fix: Folders starting with an underscore or a dot are skipped, as the research map does.

findings.defect: An owner's solution stored as v1 read back as visible to a model.
findings.scenario: Reading the committed v1 line of the owner's example gave visibility model; the model context then held the owner's example and its findings.
findings.cause: The v1 reader only rewrote the version, so visibility took its default.
findings.fix: A v1 owner_solution reads as rules_only.

findings.defect: Nothing enforced that an owner's solution is rules_only.
findings.scenario: A second owner solution built without the flag would be visible to a model.
findings.cause: The only guard was the keyword in one builder.
findings.fix: The contract refuses an owner_solution with visibility model.

findings.defect: Practice questions were indexed into their own example.
findings.scenario: The search's evaluation on the practice questions would pass by construction.
findings.cause: The search document included every practice question's words.
findings.fix: Practice questions are left out of the index.

findings.defect: How a pattern is measured was not searchable.
findings.scenario: An example whose only mention of a calibration curve was in how_to_measure was not found by those words.
findings.cause: The search document listed the other pattern fields but not how_to_measure.

findings.defect: What a role reads was not tested for names, the conversation or the storage path.
findings.scenario: Removing the exclusion of the conversation from the brief failed no test.
findings.cause: No test example carried a conversation, a name or a visible storage path.
findings.fix: A model-visible example with a name in its conversation and a path as its source; none of the three reaches the model's context.

findings.defect: A rebuild without the owner's folder dropped the owner example.
findings.scenario: In a worktree the build wrote one example fewer and the freshness test, filtering owner lines on both sides, passed.
findings.cause: The builder returned nothing when the owner's README was absent.
findings.fix: The committed owner example is carried over when the folder is absent, and the freshness test compares every line.

outcome: Every business example now says whether a model may read it; the owner's fraud solution is read by the rules only, and the one way examples reach a model drops it and keeps names, conversations and storage paths out.
lessons: A privacy flag with a permissive default must also be enforced by the contract, and old stored records must be read into the safe value.
An evaluation set must never be part of the index it evaluates.
risks: No role reads the examples yet: the check on the gateway's recorded prompts comes with 30.18.
An earlier development record quotes a column name of the owner's fraud data: the owner decides whether it stays.
